title: Cohort Gatebook: Activation Playbook & KPI Runway
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook defines a lightweight cohort-based gating system for staged activations of new product features and routing/policy changes (model pinning, quantization toggles, routing fallbacks). Aim: reduce blast radius, capture precise KPI deltas, and automate simple pass/fail gates so eng + product can move fast without manual sign-offs for every small change.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to Product Ops-managed launches where initial user population <= 100k MAU and we plan 3–5 cohort waves.
- Focus metrics: latency p95 (ms), unit cost per token (USD), error rate (% failed responses), feature adoption delta (% DAU using feature), quality regression signals (eval prompt pass rate).
- Excludes large platform changes (infra-networking, database migrations) which use SRE launch processes.

Quick overview of gating flow (one-line):
1) Canary (1% sampled cohort) -> 2) Safety ramp (1–10%) -> 3) Performance ramp (10–50%) -> 4) Open (50–100%)
Each gate is automated by a short-running check that looks at a 30–120 minute window and a 24h rolling window depending on signal stability.

Gating criteria (hard thresholds for auto-fail):
- Latency p95 increase > 50ms vs baseline (30m window) -> FAIL
- Unit cost per token increase > 20% relative to baseline (24h rolling) -> FAIL
- Error rate > 1.5x baseline or > 0.5% absolute (30m window) -> FAIL
- Quality eval pass rate drop > 5 percentage points (initial eval set) -> FAIL
- User-facing regression: >50 complaint tickets per 10k cohort users in 24h -> FAIL

Soft signals (informational, require Ops review if multiple flags):
- Small latency increase (20–50ms)
- Cost increase 10–20%
- Minor uptick in timeouts but below FAIL threshold

Critical owners and contact routing (on-call pattern):
- Product Lead (owner of feature): Priya Desai (pager/workflow notify)
- Engineering: Marco Ramirez (serving runtime) + Evan Park (platform infra)
- Product Ops: Sofia Liang (playbook steward)
- SRE escalation: sres-oncall@redwood.com (if circuit breakers trigger)

KPI runway snapshot (example table — treat as canonical tracker columns):
Columns: cohort_name | start_time | target_pct | actual_pct | latency_p95_ms | latency_delta_ms | unit_cost_usd | cost_delta_pct | error_rate_pct | quality_eval_pass_pct | tickets_per_10k | gate_decision | notes
Example rows (CSV style):
canary-2025-02-26,2025-02-26T10:00Z,1,1,210, +35, 0.00084, +12, 0.12, 92.1, 2, PASS, "minor latency bump, cost within soft limits"
safety-1,2025-02-26T14:00Z,5,4.6,230, +55, 0.00102, +22, 0.35, 90.3, 8, AUTO-FAIL, "cost exceeded 20% threshold -> rollback to canary"

How we calculate baselines (short):
- Baseline windows: 7-day rolling median for latency and cost, excluding prior experiment cohorts.
- Quality eval set: canonical 120 prompts split by intent and length (managed in product-ops repo).
- Ticket rate normalized to cohort size per 10k users.

Automations and signals (implementation notes):
- Monitoring: Redwood Console alerts (per-route) wired to the Gate Engine Lambda. Gate Engine fetches metrics from traces and token billing analyzer and runs the decision rules every 5 minutes during ramp windows.
- Rollback mechanism: automated traffic shift back to previous pinned model (or lowest-cost variant) with a 2-minute safe drain window.
- Audit: every gate decision writes an event to launch-audit-topic and creates a summary doc in the release folder.

Checklist: pre-launch (must complete before canary)
- [ ] PRs merged and e2e smoke tests passed (GH PRs linked)
- [ ] Canary traffic routing config reviewed (Marco)
- [ ] Cost model updated and validated for expected token mix (Priya + Finance)
- [ ] Eval prompts refreshed and sanity pass > 94% locally
- [ ] Runbook stub published and assigned (Product Ops)
- [ ] Customer communication draft (if external beta) prepared

Checklist: during ramp (actions owners)
- Product Ops: monitor console and callout on >2 soft flags
- Eng runtime: check logs for KV cache pressure and batching anomalies
- Infra: watch GPU queue lengths and preemptible events
- Product: verify UX surface looks correct in sampling telemetry

Contingency playbook (if AUTO-FAIL)
1) Immediate: Gate Engine triggers rollback and posts to #launch-ops with a short summary + link to audit event.
2) Triage (within 30m): Eng + Product confirm root cause hypothesis (latency vs cost vs quality). Create JIRA-incident if unknown.
3) Mitigation: If cost-driven, pin to smaller quantized model or enable aggressive caching. If latency-driven, reduce concurrency or enable lower-seq-length model variant.
4) Communication: Product Ops issues internal incident note + customer-facing update if cohort includes external users.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Do we want to weight quality eval prompts by traffic intent distribution? (PRIORITY: medium)
- Should cost threshold be dynamic by customer tier (enterprise vs free)? current system treats global -> may be too blunt.
- How to reflect downstream dependent services (e.g., reranker) in the gate decision without overloading the Gate Engine?

Post-mortem and data capture (what to store at each gate):
- Gate event payload: YAML summary with metric snapshots, top 5 traces, sample responses, feature flags at time-of-decision.
- Store a 24h sample of generation tokens (anonymized) for quality debugging (privacy filters applied).

Mini runbook for small experiments (TL;DR):
- Use canary sample size <= 1% and strict auto-fail thresholds. Keep experiment time < 2h if instability is detected. Document all changes in the release channel and attach gate event to PR.

Appendix: quick links and templates
- Gate Decision template (copy this to audit event): Title / cohort / timestamp / failing_signals / decision / owner / followups
- Slack channel: #launch-ops (for real-time)
- Runbooks: confluence:PRODOPS/COHORT-GATEBOOK-1
- Eval prompt repo: github.com/redwood-inference/evals/prompts/cohort-120

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep this doc short and iterate — the heavy rules should live in the Gate Engine code. This document is the human-readable source-of-truth for product/ops.
- Next steps: sync with SRE lead (Evan) on guardrails for GPU preempt events and add a check for GPU eviction rate in gating rules.

----
End of working draft.
